correctness.rationale: Set g(x)=x/L, u=log x, L=log u. Direct differentiation gives g'=1/L−1/(uL²) and g''=−(1−1/u−2/(uL))/(x u L²)<0 for x≥2000, confirmed by independent symbolic simplification. For r=e^{-s}, s=g'(x), x→∞, the continuous saddle height is H=g(x)−xg'( x)=x/(uL²), with log µ=H+O(1). The logarithm of coefficients minus sk has a flat block of q/10 integers near x, q=sqrt(xu)L, each within 1/100 of H, so positivity gives M/µ≥e^{-1}sqrt(xu)L/10 (conservative). Also s≥1/(2L), 1-r≥1/(4L), log A≤2H and log₂ A≤u; combining yields M/(A sqrt(log A) log₂ A)≥L/(40e sqrt2). Since log₃ A~L, the quantitative liminf follows. An exceptional set containing every sufficiently final interval has ∫dr/(1-r)=∞. Analyticity radius exactly 1 follows (a_k)^(1/k)→1, so f meets the disk assumptions. The checked saddle script only samples finite x; the proof uses the uniform Taylor and asymptotic bounds for all large x.
residual_risks: The 1/(40e√2) lower constant is conservative, not shown best.

originality.rationale: Grosse-Erdmann formulates the positive-δ iterated-logarithm disk question and discusses related entire-function endpoints. Maciá proves δ>0 disk estimates according to its abstract; the focal manuscript states Remark 5.2 leaves the δ=0 case undecided, but we could not independently read that exact remark. The present example is a precise lower-bound obstruction at δ=0 along all radii and is not implied by positive-δ upper bounds. Approval is explicitly best of knowledge with two high-relevance primary-text gaps.
residual_risks: Maciá full preprint/Remark 5.2 could not be independently read; cannot assert its entire paper does not contain an equivalent example. This alone is not a reason to call the mathematically independent example false.

value.rationale: Endpoint optimality of Wiman–Valiron disk estimates is a recognized mathematical question. The explicit positive-coefficient saddle construction resolves the first iterated-logarithm exponent-one boundary negatively with a quantitative log₃ excess, along every radius rather than a thin subsequence, so it also defeats any finite-logarithmic-measure exceptional set. This is more than a routine divergence example because the maximal-term normalization and width must balance three iterated logarithms sharply.
residual_risks: The lower constant is not optimal and does not settle endpoint hierarchies beyond n=2.

final_claim: The explicit positive-coefficient disk analytic function f(z)=Σ_{k≥2000}exp(k/log log k)z^k has M(r)/(A(r)sqrt(log A(r))*log₂ A(r))→+∞ for all r→1, with liminf after an additional log₃ A denominator at least 1/(40e sqrt2); here A=µ/(1-r). Thus the two-logarithm δ=0 endpoint cannot hold off any exceptional set of finite logarithmic measure.
limitations: Specific high-relevance primary full text Maciá 2026 and Fenton–Strumia 2009 was not read despite arXiv/OA attempts; best-of-knowledge O includes that precise priority risk.
The counterexample is analytic in the disk, unbounded, and has all positive coefficients; no optimal multiplicative constant is asserted.
